There are \(32-5=27\) students with pets. The diagram shows \(10+9+2=21\) students with exactly one pet type, leaving \(27-21=6\) with at least two types.
Counting students once per type they own gives \(32/2+(3/8)\cdot32+6=16+12+6=34\) memberships. If all six students with multiple types had exactly two, the total would be \(21+2\cdot6=33\). Each student with all three adds one more membership, so \(34-33=1\) student has all three.
